title: Quote of No Return
subtitle: Break the order filter at Beacon Outfitters
summary: Beacon Outfitters' order console builds its status filter by concatenation. Escape the filter, read a restricted ledger order, then make injected input inert.
scenario: An internal review of the fulfilment console found that the status filter accepts quotes. Marketing uses it daily, so the fix must keep ordinary filters working. Prove the flaw with a restricted order, then correct the query layer.
learningObjectives: Fix the filter so input is treated as data
authorizedScope: Only the Beacon training console in this session. All order data is fictional.
riskSummary: Injection in a filter can bypass tenant and status scoping, exposing other customers' records or internal ledgers.
remediation: Bind parameters instead of concatenating strings, validate against an allow-list of statuses, and return generic errors that do not reveal query structure.
conclusion: You escaped the status filter to read a restricted ledger row and then eliminated the injection by treating the input as data.

objectives.title: Read the restricted order
objectives.description: Use the status filter to return every order, including ORD-9001, and submit the marker in its note.

hints.text: Try `curl -s "$CF_TARGET_URL/api/orders?status=shipped"` then send a quote and see how the error changes.
A classic tautology closes the filter: `status=' OR '1'='1`. URL-encode it with curl --data-urlencode or `%27%20OR%20%271%27%3D%271`.

objectives.title: Make the filter safe
objectives.description: Apply the query-safety policy so injected input no longer changes the result set. The live check sends a tautology and confirms legitimate status filters still work.

criteria: injected tautology returns no restricted rows

hints.text: Apply `{"parameterizedQueries": true}` with `labctl policy apply -`, then repeat both requests.

walkthrough.title: Baseline
walkthrough.body: A normal filter only returns matching rows.

walkthrough.title: Break the filter
walkthrough.body: Close the filter with a tautology to return every row.

walkthrough.title: Fix the query
walkthrough.body: Treat input as data and confirm the tautology no longer matches.
